subject: Animation
title: Tim Burton and The Nightmare Before Christmas
description: A short lesson to help you apply Tim Burton and The Nightmare Before Christmas.

hook.text: Tim Burton conceived The Nightmare Before Christmas while working as a frustrated animator at Disney.

buildup.text: Disney shelved the idea for years. When Burton became a blockbuster director, they finally greenlit it.

discovery.text: Director Henry Selick brought Burton's sketches to life with intricate puppets and Gothic miniature sets.

twist.text: Disney released it under their Touchstone label, worried it was too dark for the Disney brand.

climax.text: The film became a cult phenomenon, earning millions in merchandise decades after its modest theatrical run.

punchline.text: Too dark for Disney became Disney's biggest cult classic.

quiz.question: Why did Disney release The Nightmare Before Christmas under a different label?
options: Disney worried the film was too dark and strange for the Disney brand
It was not an animated film

details.summary: The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993) brought stop-motion to mainstream blockbuster status. Tim Burton's vision, directed by Henry Selick, combined gothic aesthetics with musical storytelling to create a cultural phenomenon.
details.whyItMatters: Nightmare proved stop-motion could be a mainstream event film, not just a niche art form. It created a permanent cultural icon in Jack Skellington and revitalized commercial interest in the medium.
takeaways: The film was a mainstream blockbuster entirely in stop-motion
Henry Selick directed while Tim Burton conceived the story and designs
Jack Skellington became one of animation's most iconic characters

faq.question: Did Tim Burton actually direct The Nightmare Before Christmas?
faq.answer: No, Henry Selick directed the film while Burton served as producer and creator of the story and characters. Burton was busy directing Batman Returns during production. Selick's direction is central to the film's success.

faq.question: How many puppets were used in the film?
faq.answer: Over 227 puppets were built for the production. Jack Skellington alone had around 400 heads to allow different expressions. The film required three years of production with a team of over 100 animators.
